messages.subject: Consumable Resource
parts:
Has anyone worked with a supply chain simulation involving deliveries and consumption of a consumable resource, such as manufacturing parts or material? 

I thought of a couple of ways to do this, but am unsure about how accurate they are and was wondering if there's a more straightforward way. 

One way was to set the resource capacity to the cumulative sum of deliveries and have arrivals seize but never release capacity at the resource. 

Another was to modify the capacity by +1 with another generator on schedule with deliveries and then when an arrival intending to use the resource comes along it seizes, releases and then modifies the resources capacity by -1.

Thanks for the help!

On Tue, 26 Mar 2019 at 17:04, Bridget <bbas...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Has anyone worked with a supply chain simulation involving deliveries and consumption of a consumable resource, such as manufacturing parts or material?
>
> I thought of a couple of ways to do this, but am unsure about how accurate they are and was wondering if there's a more straightforward way.
>
> One way was to set the resource capacity to the cumulative sum of deliveries and have arrivals seize but never release capacity at the resource.
>
> Another was to modify the capacity by +1 with another generator on schedule with deliveries and then when an arrival intending to use the resource comes along it seizes, releases and then modifies the resources capacity by -1.

Currently, this second method is the proper way to do it, because, if
you don't release resources, you'll get a bunch of warnings.

There's an open issue [1] that plans the addition of new resource
types: containers and stores, which would be the most accurate pattern
here. But since this is already doable with the procedure you
described above, it's not in my priority list.

[1] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/120
